# Startup readback: AI-28

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Harden the existing Apple/mobile input path so a paired device can submit supported Health, Calendar, Reminder and other retained mobile snapshots safely, with reliable replay handling, deterministic canonical adaptation, and trustworthy provenance/freshness. Apple is input-only: Calendar/Reminder writes remain with Google under AI-27/AI-30.

1. Only a currently valid, scoped, non-revoked device can submit a rate-limited, bounded, supported versioned snapshot. Reminder records use contract v2 and identify their list; a missing or device-disabled list fails closed before any snapshot or raw record is retained. Malformed, incompatible, excessive, wrong-token, and revoked submissions fail closed with redacted actionable errors.
2. Replaying a request, snapshot, or typed source record creates no duplicate canonical record. Accepted Health/Calendar/Reminder inputs map deterministically to canonical domain data while retaining an immutable raw-evidence link, source/device, hashes, capture and ingest timestamps, adaptation state, and freshness.
3. A partial adapter failure leaves the raw snapshot available and the failure observable/retryable; retry produces one canonical result. Updated snapshots adapt only changed/new records and freshness changes follow captured data rather than upload time alone.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

- Blocking contracts are complete: AI-12 is Done (PR #162) and defines explicit endpoint authentication; AI-19 is Done (PR #171; shared integration skill PR #172) and defines evidence/provenance/freshness/trace conventions. AI-11 is Done (PRs #158 and #161) and supplies the exposed-table RLS/Data API pattern. These are completion references, not permission to broaden grants.
- AI-27 is related, not blocking. Its issue amendment makes Apple input-only; Google Calendar/Tasks owns planner output. AI-30 is likewise not a dependency for Apple writes.
- Interfaces to verify before implementation: the existing `mobile-snapshot-ingest`/Apple bridge Edge ingress, device registration/token issue and revoke path, snapshot/raw-evidence storage (including R2 for payloads too large for efficient DB retention), typed record tables and deterministic Health/Calendar/Reminder adapters. The supported Shortcut path uses `mobile-snapshot-ingest`; MFA-gated pairing/revocation is handled by `apple-bridge-device`. `apple-bridge-ingest` is a separate legacy ingress and `health-ingest` is reserved for the future official bulk exporter. Keep those contracts distinct unless issue evidence identifies a defect in them.
- Production Health data is sensitive. Tests and staging evidence must use synthetic fixtures; never copy production personal data, plaintext credentials, or raw Health payloads into source, routine logs, screenshots, or the ticket.

## Implementation and boundaries

The required `corepack pnpm qa:doctor --fix` passed in this isolated worktree before feature inspection. Trace the existing producer → authenticated Edge route → persisted raw batch/source records → canonical adapter → downstream Health consumer. Make only the demonstrated changes needed for scoped revocable device auth, versioned typed validation, request/snapshot/source-record idempotency, deterministic adaptation, freshness/provenance, and safe partial retry. Preserve existing route/auth contracts, RLS and restricted database caller roles; inspect all direct producers and consumers before changing a boundary. The scoped Reminder contract requires list identity in the input, server rejection before raw persistence when missing or disabled, and typed provenance of the list. Add a migration only if current schema evidence requires it and use the coordinated prefix `20261021155521`.

Do not introduce Apple private API scraping, plaintext-token retrieval, broad `service_role`/Data API grants, account-wide data capture, Calendar/Reminder writeback, duplicate canonical stores, or a new ingestion framework. Keep the manual one-file upload fallback where the Build Spec requires it. No subagents are planned; this is one owner from implementation through release.

Integration contract: use the existing device-authenticated Apple/mobile snapshot ingress and its least-privilege database path; carry DB-03/DB-05/DB-10 for migrations, SQL persistence and versioned idempotent replay, EDGE-01/EDGE-02 if Edge imports or test-source staging change, OPS-01 for actionable redacted failures, and ACC-01/ACC-02 for hosted evidence and any real MFA checkpoint. The v2 replay test exposed a duplicate same-record/version adaptation insert; DB-10 and AI28-01 record the confirmed cause and prevention.

## Hosted proof and readiness

This issue explicitly requires live staging sign-off because a real supported shortcut/device request crosses the deployed endpoint and storage boundary. After exact-head candidate readiness and a serialized staging lease, use a staging device and synthetic/non-personal fixture data to perform the eight issue checks: valid submission through the supported pairing path; raw/source/canonical/provenance/freshness verification; identical replay; changed/new snapshot; revoke then deny with no writes; malformed/oversize/wrong-token denials with redacted diagnostics; forced adapter failure and safe retry; freshness aging/update transition. Record redacted artifact references only. The operator must perform Apple Shortcut/Health Export authorization. If a headed login/MFA prompt appears, stop and ask the operator once that browser is ready; do not fabricate sign-off.

Before dispatch, validate the local DB application-role/RPC/column grants and fixtures, then dry-run the existing acceptance evidence producer → validator → consumer. Confirm the candidate SHA, deployment provenance, profile and lease match the exact head.

## Delegation and blockers

One owner handles all implementation and release evidence. QA doctor has passed. Current blocker is only shared local Supabase/browser serialization: parent holds the lease for AI-20. Resume boundary proofs after explicit lease release; staging remains a later serialized external proof. If headed login/MFA is needed, pause before sign-in and notify the parent so the operator can authorize when the browser is ready.

Linear agent-context lookup was attempted for mobile ingestion but the connector returned `Tool get_agent_context not found`; its agent-skill list is empty. Continue from the issue, completed dependency evidence, repository specs, and integration rules.

## Remaining-work readback · 22 Oct 2026

The existing PR is #180 at `5b522b2c114f0333fe503a471d5249a721d17109` (base `5e898c1d574feee944b95481c3e7ecd6482adde0`). Its latest hosted boundary run `39644833934` did not fail on image pulls: retries completed and the database/backfill suites passed (27 files / 506 assertions; the legacy AI-14 backfill passed 4/4). The run then failed at `corepack pnpm environment:drift -- repo-local`: generated `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` differs semantically from the fully migrated schema. Correction to the previous checkpoint: read-only name scans show all RPCs previously listed are still present in the candidate; that absence claim was wrong. The candidate types do add `ComputedFields: never` across table shapes and reorder function declarations. The AI-28 migration does not drop or replace functions. CI observed 1311 public columns; the earlier successful local drift report recorded 1310. Generator-version skew is a concrete hypothesis, not yet confirmed as the semantic mismatch cause. Update · 22 Oct 2026: root cause confirmed. QA doctor accepted installed Supabase CLI 2.120.0 although `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins 2.118.0; generation with the mismatched binary caused repo-local schema drift. A frozen install restored 2.118.0, and regenerating types from the fully migrated schema made `corepack pnpm environment:drift -- repo-local` pass (1,311 public columns; digest `e869e6e0392d81fde1232b953ef18fb584a2ce3997ad1103d127e0ec95cf840a`). The doctor now checks the exact lockfile version and `--fix` performs the frozen install on mismatch; focused regression tests and DB-04/AI28-02 document the prevention. Next run the changed-surface gate, push and verify exact-head CI. Real Apple Shortcut/device acceptance remains an operator gate; no staging/MFA is being requested in this pass.
